inputs.title: The Box That Felt Small
inputs.logline: After Jenny hides the shame of misreading a word, Patch leads the Box Monsters into a shoebox classroom where a giant mistake must become something she can try again with, not something that makes her small.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny stands at the front of the classroom holding her worksheet.
The word BRIDGE is written on the board.
Jenny looks at the word. Her fingers tighten around the paper.
One child lets out a tiny laugh. Another child laughs because the first one did.
Jenny looks at the word again. It feels much bigger now.
Final Frame: Jenny frozen, embarrassed, holding the worksheet close.

beats.storyBeat: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corrected answer come out small.
beats.want: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn.
beats.need: She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth.
beats.kidRead: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it.
beats.adultRead: A small public stumble can become disproportionately huge inside a sensitive child, even when the adults respond gently.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson.

orderedEvents.text: Shot 03: The Feeling Goes Into The Box
Jenny kneels on her bedroom floor.
Her decorated shoebox sits beside her bed. It has stars, hearts and one wonky rainbow drawn on the lid.
Inside are small treasures: a ribbon, a pebble, an old badge, a folded card.
She places the folded worksheet inside the box.
For a moment, she keeps her hand on it.

beats.storyBeat: In her bedroom, Jenny brings the folded worksheet to her decorated shoebox, a safe place for treasured things. She tries to make the feeling disappear by placing it inside and closing the lid, not noticing that the box has received more than paper: it has received the feeling she cannot carry alone.
beats.want: Jenny wants to put the worksheet away and stop thinking about the classroom mistake.
beats.need: She needs the hidden feeling to be met, not buried.
beats.kidRead: Jenny hides the paper because looking at it hurts.
beats.adultRead: The shoebox becomes a child’s private emotional container: a tender coping strategy that also signals isolation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the action intimate and gentle, with the box feeling like a confidant even before the magic answers.

direction.premise: A classroom reading mistake follows Jenny home until her shoebox calls the Box Monsters into a handmade shame world built around one too-large wrong word.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can the monsters help Jenny carry the mistake differently before shame makes her feel too small to try again?
direction.theme: Getting something wrong does not make you small.
direction.externalJourney: Jenny misreads a word, hides the worksheet in her shoebox, and the monsters travel from The Fold into a cardboard classroom where the mistaken word has swollen into the room’s bossy centrepiece. Their attempted fix fails, then they transform the machine and the meaning of the mistake so Jenny can face the word again.
direction.internalJourney: Jenny moves from public embarrassment, to hiding, to a tiny private openness, to reclaiming the mistake with humour, and finally to trying again while still feeling nervous.
direction.relationshipChanges: Patch begins as a brave responder who wants to help quickly, but earns Jenny’s echo’s trust by sitting with her instead of fixing her. Tilly shifts from controlling the outcome to redesigning her solution around emotional truth. Rumble protects space rather than forcing confidence. Nib’s odd humour becomes the safe bridge between shame and self-acceptance.
direction.emotionalCurve: Quiet pressure builds into embarrassment, then withdrawal, then magical concern. The middle tightens as the wrong fix makes shame heavier. Relief arrives first through being met gently, then through laughter that belongs to Jenny rather than at Jenny. The ending lands in soft courage and secret warmth.
direction.comedyCurve: The comedy starts as character imbalance in The Fold, turns into dry diagnosis and wonky tools, dips during the failed fix, then returns as Nib’s sideways cafe idea makes the mistake feel usable rather than poisonous. The final joke is small, affectionate and earned.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The word BRIDGE becomes BRIGGLE in class, then grows into the shame world’s looming word, then shrinks through laughter, becomes BRIDGE again, and returns in the classroom as a word Jenny can say. Jenny folds the worksheet smaller when ashamed, then later carries it without folding it. The Correct Answer Machine fails, then becomes the Try Again Machine. The shoebox’s first sigh and call pay off as its warm twitch and The Fold lamp glow.

direction.premise: A classroom reading mistake follows Jenny home until her shoebox calls the Box Monsters into a handmade shame world built around one too-large wrong word.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can the monsters help Jenny carry the mistake differently before shame makes her feel too small to try again?
direction.theme: Getting something wrong does not make you small.
direction.externalJourney: Jenny misreads a word, hides the worksheet in her shoebox, and the monsters travel from The Fold into a cardboard classroom where the mistaken word has swollen into the room’s bossy centrepiece. Their attempted fix fails, then they transform the machine and the meaning of the mistake so Jenny can face the word again.
direction.internalJourney: Jenny moves from public embarrassment, to hiding, to a tiny private openness, to reclaiming the mistake with humour, and finally to trying again while still feeling nervous.
direction.relationshipChanges: Patch begins as a brave responder who wants to help quickly, but earns Jenny’s echo’s trust by sitting with her instead of fixing her. Tilly shifts from controlling the outcome to redesigning her solution around emotional truth. Rumble protects space rather than forcing confidence. Nib’s odd humour becomes the safe bridge between shame and self-acceptance.
direction.emotionalCurve: Quiet pressure builds into embarrassment, then withdrawal, then magical concern. The middle tightens as the wrong fix makes shame heavier. Relief arrives first through being met gently, then through laughter that belongs to Jenny rather than at Jenny. The ending lands in soft courage and secret warmth.
direction.comedyCurve: The comedy starts as character imbalance in The Fold, turns into dry diagnosis and wonky tools, dips during the failed fix, then returns as Nib’s sideways cafe idea makes the mistake feel usable rather than poisonous. The final joke is small, affectionate and earned.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The word BRIDGE becomes BRIGGLE in class, then grows into the shame world’s looming word, then shrinks through laughter, becomes BRIDGE again, and returns in the classroom as a word Jenny can say. Jenny folds the worksheet smaller when ashamed, then later carries it without folding it. The Correct Answer Machine fails, then becomes the Try Again Machine. The shoebox’s first sigh and call pay off as its warm twitch and The Fold lamp glow.
direction.visualMotifs: Folding paper as shrinking self-worth; oversized lettering as shame taking up too much space; golden tape and cards as repair, not erasure; cardboard walls pressing inward and later opening with warmth; the shoebox as a private container that becomes a gentle doorway.
direction.sonicMotifs: Classroom quiet, tiny laugh, bell, cardboard sigh, pulse through floorboards, Fold honk, echoing repeated mistake, clunking machine, soft laugh, warm final glow.
direction.climax: Patch names the emotional truth that being wrong did not make Jenny small, allowing Tilly to change the machine’s purpose and Jenny’s echo to receive the golden repair card.
direction.resolution: Jenny wakes to the repaired worksheet and card, returns to class, reads the line correctly, gently jokes about the earlier mistake, and smiles as the secret magic remains unseen.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: A warm, private courage: the feeling is still remembered, but it is no longer bigger than Jenny.

showrunnerJudgement: PASS. I tried to break it on the main danger points: comedy overwhelming shame, Patch becoming only a loud leader, the alarm feeling like a gag instead of a call, and the route becoming action-padding. The scene holds. The accumulated behaviour makes the turn visible: Patch’s performed height collapses, Tilly names the call plainly, Rumble’s question creates space, and the team’s stillness after “Shame” earns the quieter mission. The audience can laugh at the cardboard wobble, then feel the room lower its voice. Patch’s change is readable in action, not speech alone: he gives up the tower pose and leads with soft rules and forward motion. One important beat remains legible muted and in silhouette/staging: the stack collapse followed by the grouped stillness around the call strip clearly shows the move from silly imbalance to careful attention.
treatmentComparison: The storyboard stays close to the selected whole-scene treatment. Shot 05 delivers the Fold alarm interrupting Patch and Nib’s routine, and it protects the required temperature drop when Tilly reads “Shame.” Shot 06 carries the intended soft-mission contradiction: Patch sets gentle rules, Tilly punctures his history, Nib runs ahead ridiculous but useful, and the group enters the route with concern rather than panic. The central audience experience is intact: funny cardboard city, serious feeling named, then rescue momentum with handmade wonkiness and tenderness. The treatment’s emotional argument — shame needs steadiness, space, and no big fixing — is visible in the staging and voice plan.
